name: The Tara CPA Firm
signal: Keep More Money podcast and fit-call funnel
services: The firm markets ongoing planning, federal and state preparation, quarterly estimates and strategy calls for profitable entrepreneurs.
focus: a recurring advisor relationship for a profitable service business
scenario: A consultant has growing profit, irregular owner draws and a spouse with employment income. Last year's estimates no longer reflect the household. The next decision is how to update the projection before another large client payment arrives.
risk: A regular meeting is useful only if the numbers feeding it are current. Determine who updates the projection after a significant income change and how the owner learns that a payment needs attention.
questions: What triggers a new estimate between scheduled meetings?
Which spouse and outside-income records enter the projection?
Who records completed actions after a strategy call?
records: Current profit and loss and open receivables
Owner draws and payroll year to date
deliverable: a dated household projection with an income-change trigger and next payment instructions
switch: uncertainty about quarterly payments rather than a desire to replace otherwise reliable bookkeeping
alternative: Request an estimate-review engagement first if your current preparer already has accurate records. A broader planning relationship becomes more useful when income changes repeatedly require decisions throughout the year.

name: Fraim, Cawley & Company CPAs
signal: NFIB Ask the CPA webinar and business-advice content
services: Its practice lists tax preparation, advisory, bookkeeping, business valuation, forensic accounting and exit planning.
focus: an owner preparing financial records and an exit discussion
scenario: An owner has received an unsolicited acquisition inquiry but has never reconciled personal expenses, related-party rent and discretionary compensation. The immediate job is preparing a consistent earnings picture before discussing a purchase price.
risk: Valuation, deal negotiation and tax modeling are different assignments. An exit proposal should identify who prepares the earnings adjustments and who reviews transaction assumptions with legal counsel.
questions: Is valuation included or a separately commissioned report?
Who reconciles historical earnings adjustments to filed returns?
When does the tax advisor review proposed transaction terms?
records: Three years of returns and financial statements
Draft buyer inquiry or proposed terms
deliverable: an agreed earnings reconciliation and a separate transaction-review timetable
switch: a potential sale that requires work beyond the current annual filing process
alternative: Keep the existing preparer for open returns while commissioning a defined exit-readiness project. If valuation or forensic work is required, compare providers qualified for that specific assignment before selecting the owner tax planner.

name: Wellness Fi
signal: Therapist-focused bookkeeping guides and tiered consultation offers
services: Wellness Fi lists quarterly or monthly bookkeeping, practice advisory, estimates and tax strategy. Annual filing can be added; its published scope treats other businesses, property and cleanup as additional work.
focus: choosing the reporting and advisory cadence for a mental-health practice
scenario: A therapist sees steady patient demand but is unsure whether monthly accounting is needed. A second revenue stream and a rental property have also appeared. The decision is which recurring practice services to buy and which outside activities need their own scope.
risk: A practice bundle can be a good fit without covering every household activity. Quote the practice work separately from the new business and property so the owner can see which records and fees belong to each.
questions: What changes when I move from quarterly to monthly reporting?
How are non-practice businesses and rentals priced?
Is annual filing included in this exact proposal?
deliverable: a reporting-cadence recommendation and separate scope for each income source
switch: outgrowing a practice-only bundle while still valuing its recurring bookkeeping
alternative: A specialist planning engagement can complement the practice bookkeeper. Compare a full migration only after the proposed replacement explains how clinical receipts, business records and household information will be reconciled.

name: Taxhub
signal: Tax calculators and direct online preparation and consultation offers
services: The US Taxhub site lists tax preparation, consultation, bookkeeping, S-corporation conversion and Form 5472 filing. This comparison concerns gettaxhub.com, not similarly named overseas providers.
focus: online preparation with a clearly scoped consultation
scenario: An independent professional needs a business return prepared and wants to discuss a possible entity change. The owner also receives a partnership K-1. The practical question is whether one proposal covers preparation, the decision analysis and the subsequent implementation.
risk: An available consultation does not automatically establish the deliverables of an entity project. Obtain the analysis, filing assignments and ongoing payroll responsibilities before treating a conversion as completed.
questions: Which planning deliverables accompany my preparation quote?
Who completes the entity-change implementation tasks?
How will a late K-1 affect my filing and estimates?
records: Current entity documents and prior elections
deliverable: a preparation scope plus a separate entity-decision work plan
switch: wanting implementation clarity beyond a convenient filing workflow
alternative: If preparation works well, keep it and add a decision-specific consultation. If several entities and personal investments need coordinated review, request a planning proposal that names all of them rather than adding isolated calls one at a time.

name: Collective
signal: S-corporation calculators, guides and plan-selection funnels
services: Collective markets a subscription back office for self-employed owners, including bookkeeping and tax support. Its S-corporation offering includes entity-return and payroll-related services; confirm partner roles and personal-return coverage in the selected plan.
focus: administration for a business of one
scenario: A solo designer wants less administration but has just added a second business and purchased a rental. The question is whether the existing subscription still fits the owner's complete situation or whether a separate planning relationship is needed.
risk: Convenience within one workflow can conceal work outside it. Make a list of every return and decision before assuming one monthly charge covers the second activity, rental records and household planning.
questions: Does this plan cover each entity and my rental activity?
Which professional signs each return and reviews planning?
What happens to payroll and ledger access when I leave?
deliverable: an entity-by-entity coverage map and an exportable implementation record
switch: expanding beyond a single-owner administrative workflow
alternative: Retain a convenient back office while commissioning coordinated owner planning if the services can exchange complete records. A full replacement should explain how bookkeeping, payroll, return preparation and decision review continue without gaps.

name: Xendoo
signal: Free books-review offers, calculators and a resource hub
services: Xendoo publishes online bookkeeping, catch-up work, financial reporting and CPA-delivered tax planning and filing, alongside dashboard-based financial insights.
focus: repairing bookkeeping and connecting regular reports with taxes
scenario: An online seller has deposits from several channels but cannot reconcile refunds, processor fees and transfers. Tax planning has stalled because reported profit changes every time the ledger is reviewed. Reliable books are the first dependency.
risk: A tax recommendation based on unreconciled payouts may need revision. Define the cleanup completion standard before using the ledger to project income or approve owner distributions.
questions: Who reconciles processor settlements and refunds?
What constitutes an accepted catch-up close?
How do corrected books flow into the next projection?
records: Prior ledger and filed business returns
deliverable: a reconciled opening balance and a documented books-to-tax handoff
switch: needing reliable numbers before buying additional strategy work
alternative: Commission bookkeeping cleanup before changing the tax advisor if record quality is the bottleneck. When comparing bundled providers, ask to see the proposed reconciliation process and the first month in which planning can use accepted numbers.

name: Pilot
signal: Tax-provider selection webinars and startup finance content
services: Pilot publishes business tax preparation and filing alongside bookkeeping and broader financial-management services. Pilot.com is distinct from the CPA Pilot software already covered elsewhere on this site.
focus: a startup's business filing and finance workflow
scenario: A founder is moving from initial bookkeeping to investor reporting. Corporate deadlines, employee payments and the founder's personal investments are now being discussed together. The owner needs to know where the company engagement ends and personal advice begins.
risk: A company finance workflow and a founder's household return can have different responsible professionals. Separate corporate compliance, management reporting and owner planning before evaluating the total quote.
questions: Which corporate jurisdictions and filings are included?
How are founder personal questions scoped?
Who reconciles the tax return with investor-facing reports?
deliverable: a corporate compliance calendar with a separate founder-planning assignment
switch: adding personal complexity to an otherwise useful company finance system
alternative: Keep startup accounting if it meets reporting needs and add a founder tax planner for outside activities. Compare a replacement only when it can explain the corporate calendar and preserve the reporting investors already rely on.

name: Decimal
signal: Small-business tax resources and consultation offers
services: Decimal lists federal and state preparation, planning, estimates and entity guidance for small and midsize businesses. Its tax service materials discuss working with clean books, including records maintained elsewhere.
focus: connecting an existing ledger to a tax engagement
scenario: A home-services owner likes the current bookkeeper but wants a more deliberate tax process. Seasonal income and equipment purchases make last year's payments a poor planning reference. Replacing the ledger provider may be unnecessary.
risk: A new advisor needs an accepted data cutoff and a correction process. Specify who resolves coding questions and how later ledger adjustments affect a projection that has already been delivered.
questions: Can you use my existing bookkeeper's records?
Who resolves ledger corrections before filing?
How are seasonal changes reflected in estimates?
records: Monthly financial statements and general ledger
deliverable: a books-acceptance checklist and seasonal estimate update schedule
switch: improving tax coordination while keeping a working accounting process
alternative: Compare tax-only or planning-only proposals before buying a bundled accounting replacement. If record delays repeatedly prevent review, include a monthly close service in the shortlist and specify the date the tax team receives usable reports.

name: Fondo
signal: TaxPass landing pages and a founder QSBS questionnaire
services: Fondo markets startup bookkeeping, tax filing and tax-credit work. TaxPass describes corporate federal and state returns, Delaware franchise-tax work and separately scoped international additions.
focus: startup corporate compliance and founder record readiness
scenario: A small startup has raised capital and the founder has heard about stock-related tax planning. Corporate filings still need completion. The first task is collecting ownership and issuance records rather than treating a questionnaire result as a personal tax conclusion.
risk: A screening tool cannot replace review of actual ownership history. Ask who performs founder-level analysis, what assumptions are tested and whether that work is separate from corporate filing.
questions: Which founder-level stock questions are included?
What records support any stock-treatment analysis?
How are international additions scoped and assigned?
deliverable: a corporate filing calendar and a separately documented founder-record review
switch: requiring individual planning beyond a startup compliance package
alternative: Pair a functioning corporate tax service with a specialist owner engagement if responsibilities can be defined cleanly. An alternative should identify the exact stock records it needs and avoid promising a result before reviewing them.

name: Kruze Consulting
signal: Extensive startup finance and tax question-and-answer library
services: Kruze markets tax services for venture-backed startups, with accounting and financial-support work positioned around funding and growth stages.
focus: venture-backed company reporting and compliance
scenario: A founder's company needs finance support for a funding round while the founder is buying an investment property. These are simultaneous decisions with different evidence and stakeholders. A proposal should separate company reporting from personal acquisition planning.
risk: Investor-facing company work should not be displaced simply because the founder's personal tax needs changed. Clarify who receives business information and which professional coordinates household decisions.
questions: What reporting work is required for this funding stage?
Is founder personal-property planning included?
How are company and owner advisors permitted to exchange records?
records: Funding documents and investor reporting calendar
Property purchase documents and personal returns
deliverable: separate corporate and owner workstreams with a named coordination contact
switch: adding property or household planning to a venture-backed finance arrangement
alternative: Maintain startup finance support when it serves the board and commission owner planning separately. If seeking a single replacement, require evidence that it can meet investor reporting requirements as well as the owner's individual assignment.

name: Heard
signal: Private-practice marketing webinars and tiered plan offers
services: Heard markets a financial platform and professional support for therapists, including bookkeeping, estimates and plan-dependent annual filing. Payroll and some tax services depend on the chosen plan or add-ons.
focus: a therapist selecting a platform and support tier
scenario: A solo therapist is preparing to hire clinicians and move from a simple practice to a group. The owner must decide whether a plan upgrade covers new payroll and business-return responsibilities or whether additional advisory work is required.
risk: Plan names do not establish identical tax coverage. Compare the actual business return, personal return, payroll and support entitlements of the proposal that applies after the first hire.
questions: Which filings and advice are available on this tier?
What changes when I hire my first clinician?
How do payroll and catch-up charges affect first-year cost?
records: Practice entity status and previous returns
Current books and platform export options
deliverable: a first-hire responsibility checklist and a complete first-year service quote
switch: needing a clearer transition from solo to group-practice administration
alternative: Compare a plan upgrade with a practice-focused accounting engagement before migrating. Add owner planning separately when outside businesses or property create questions beyond the practice workflow, and confirm data access in either arrangement.

name: Acuity
signal: Industry landing pages, financial guides and demo funnels
services: Acuity publishes bookkeeping, accounting, tax and CFO services with configurable support by business stage. Current site materials identify Acuity as powered by Sorren; confirm the contracting entity and professional responsibilities.
focus: a growing company needing configurable accounting support
scenario: An ecommerce brand has outgrown owner-managed books and needs inventory reporting, sales-channel reconciliation and income-tax work. The owner also wants personal planning. One engagement may handle operations while another handles the household.
risk: Sales-tax compliance, inventory accounting and income-tax planning use related records but remain separate responsibilities. Ask each proposal to assign these workstreams and name the professional reviewing owner-level decisions.
questions: Who handles inventory adjustments and channel reconciliation?
Which sales-tax tasks are included alongside income taxes?
Which legal entity contracts for each service?
records: Entity returns and owner income records
deliverable: a staged accounting roadmap with separate tax and owner-planning assignments
switch: needing operational finance depth alongside personal tax coordination
alternative: Compare an accounting upgrade with a full-service replacement. If the accounting team already delivers reliable reports, use those reports for a separate owner-planning engagement rather than duplicating the monthly close.

name: Tax Hack Accounting Group
signal: Digital-business service content and consultation funnel
services: Tax Hack describes tax advisory and compliance for internet, software and ecommerce businesses, with a portal and recurring planning meetings.
focus: tax support organized around a digital business
scenario: A software owner has contractors in several places and is increasing development spending. The owner wants to understand which activities require specialized review and how recurring planning connects with return preparation.
risk: An industry label is useful context but does not define the evidence needed for a specific project. Require the provider to identify missing records, any specialist work and the implementation deadline before relying on projected benefits.
questions: Which contractor and development records must be reviewed?
What is included in recurring meetings versus separate projects?
Who approves the final technical position and supporting file?
deliverable: a record-request matrix and an agreed specialist-review sequence
switch: seeking clearer documentation for software-business decisions
alternative: Add a defined technical review if the current tax process works but a new project requires more evidence. Compare recurring advisory providers when decisions arise frequently and the same records must be updated throughout the year.

name: JETRO and Associates
signal: Gym-focused articles and a niche online service funnel
services: JETRO's fitness site publishes remote bookkeeping, year-round tax planning, annual preparation and payroll for gym and studio owners.
focus: the recurring back office of a gym or fitness studio
scenario: A first-location gym owner has trainers, membership receipts and payroll deadlines but no reliable monthly reporting. The owner wants an advisor who can help establish routine records before discussing a property purchase.
risk: Recurring payroll and membership administration cannot pause during a tax-advisor change. A transition proposal should preserve employee payments and define which closing month becomes the new team's responsibility.
questions: How are membership receipts reconciled each month?
Who owns payroll filing deadlines during transition?
When can a property acquisition enter planning?
deliverable: a first monthly close calendar and an uninterrupted payroll handoff
switch: needing a fitness-specific operating workflow before broader owner planning
alternative: Compare a gym-focused bookkeeping and payroll service with adding tax planning to existing operations. Where a property decision is the new requirement, a separately scoped planner may complement the fitness back office without moving payroll.

name: Vincere Tax
signal: Financial-planner partnership landing pages and tax blog
services: Vincere lists tax preparation, planning, consulting, representation and bookkeeping. It also advertises white-label tax services for financial-planning practices.
focus: tax coordination through a financial-planner relationship
scenario: An owner already uses a financial planner and wants business tax work integrated with that relationship. A liquidity event is approaching. The owner needs to know who makes the tax recommendation, who communicates it and who implements the agreed action.
risk: A familiar advisory brand can front a different tax-service provider. The engagement should identify the tax professional, permissions for information sharing and the party responsible for direct client follow-up.
questions: Who contracts with me and signs the tax work?
Can I speak directly with the assigned tax professional?
How are planning instructions exchanged with my financial planner?
deliverable: a communication map naming the tax reviewer and implementation owners
switch: wanting direct accountability within an existing advisor network
alternative: Compare a planner-coordinated tax relationship with hiring an independent tax advisor who collaborates with the planner. Require the same records, consent process and decision timetable so branding does not obscure responsibility.

name: Little Fish Accounting
signal: Build to Enough podcast and service-application funnel
services: Little Fish publishes accounting, tax support and advisory for service-based businesses with small teams, with ongoing bookkeeping positioned as part of its service model.
focus: sustainable growth for a small service-business team
scenario: An agency owner is deciding whether to add a team member or keep the company deliberately small. The owner needs accurate profit and a household tax projection before choosing a sustainable compensation target.
risk: Revenue growth does not automatically improve owner cash availability. Ask the advisor to distinguish a hiring forecast, the company's reported profit and the household payment estimate rather than using one number for all three.
questions: Which reports support a hiring decision?
How are owner draws distinguished from business profit?
Who updates household estimates after staffing changes?
records: Proposed employee cost and payroll timing
Owner income targets and current estimates
deliverable: a staffing decision brief tied to separate business and household forecasts
switch: wanting decisions connected to the owner's preferred business size
alternative: Compare ongoing advisory accounting with a narrower tax-planning engagement if the records are already dependable. The proposal should respond to the owner's goals, including a deliberate choice to limit growth, rather than assuming expansion is always the objective.

name: The Bottom Line CPA
signal: Profit First positioning, client education and consultation offers
services: The Bottom Line CPA markets financial and tax services with a Profit First emphasis, a dedicated profit-and-tax team and secure client communication.
focus: cash allocation alongside accounting and tax support
scenario: A profitable owner uses separate cash accounts but still receives unexpected tax-payment instructions. The next question is whether allocation percentages are being reconciled with a current projection and the owner's outside income.
risk: Cash set aside is a funding decision; projected liability is an analysis based on records. Ask how the two are reconciled when profit, payroll or household income changes rather than assuming the bank balance proves adequate preparation.
questions: How are reserve transfers checked against projected payments?
What happens when the owner changes compensation?
Who reconciles business allocations with household obligations?
deliverable: a reserve-to-projection reconciliation with clear update triggers
switch: needing more clarity between a cash system and tax obligations
alternative: Keep a useful cash-allocation system while requesting a documented projection review. Compare broader advisory relationships if the owner also needs recurring interpretation of profit, compensation and available cash before making decisions.

name: The Fitness CPA
signal: Fitness revenue and franchise guides with niche consultation offers
services: The Fitness CPA markets accounting, taxes, payroll and financial operations for fitness businesses, with franchise and expansion-related advisory materials.
focus: financial decisions around a fitness-business expansion
scenario: A studio owner is evaluating a second location and new equipment financing. The tax advisor needs to coordinate the opening budget, staffing plan and owner cash requirements before any forecast is treated as a green light to expand.
risk: A location forecast and an owner tax plan serve different decisions. Compare who reviews lease commitments, cash runway and tax timing, and specify whether financing assumptions are tested or merely accepted from the owner.
questions: Who reviews the second-location forecast?
How do equipment commitments enter planning?
Which payroll and reporting tasks continue through opening?
records: First-location reports and owner income needs
deliverable: an expansion-readiness work plan with a separate owner payment projection
switch: requiring coordinated review before committing to a second studio
alternative: Compare fitness-focused operational advisory with adding an owner tax planner to the existing team. A replacement should preserve location-level reports and explain the evidence needed before supporting an expansion decision.

name: Accountfully
signal: Downloadable tax and investor guides and industry landing pages
services: Accountfully publishes bookkeeping, accounting, tax planning and filing for businesses, including consumer brands. BELAY acquired Accountfully in 2025; verify the current service brand and contracting arrangements.
focus: financial reporting for a consumer-products business
scenario: A small packaged-goods brand is growing wholesale orders while inventory absorbs cash. The owner wants tax planning but also needs reliable product margins and lender-ready records. These assignments should be priced and scheduled separately.
risk: A business can report earnings while struggling to fund inventory. Ask the provider to separate inventory accounting, operating cash forecasting and tax projections so each decision uses the right report.
questions: Who reconciles inventory and product cost?
Which reports are prepared for lenders or investors?
What is the current contracting and service arrangement?
deliverable: an inventory-close schedule with separate lender and tax reporting outputs
switch: seeking deeper consumer-brand reporting alongside owner planning
alternative: Compare an inventory-capable accounting provider with retaining the ledger team and adding owner tax planning. Confirm how the current service organization handles access, continuity and responsibilities before migrating records.

name: Blumer CPAs
signal: Entrepreneur-focused resources and growth-advisory positioning
services: Blumer lists accounting, tax, payroll and advisory for entrepreneurs, with service-business and creative-agency positioning and growth-related consulting.
focus: an agency's financial model and owner decision process
scenario: A creative agency has profitable projects but uneven capacity and partner compensation. The owners want to change the delivery model before year-end. Tax planning needs to work from the revised business assumptions rather than last year's structure.
risk: Business-model consulting and tax implementation may require different deliverables. Specify who updates the staffing and margin assumptions and who turns the approved operating model into a tax-review brief.
questions: What operating-model work is included in advisory?
How are partner compensation changes reviewed?
Who tracks implementation after a consulting session?
deliverable: an approved operating-assumption set and a linked tax-action schedule
switch: changing the agency model while retaining financial accountability
alternative: Compare agency advisory accounting with a decision-specific tax engagement. If the business model still needs work, resolve those assumptions first; a tax projection based on an unapproved staffing plan can create false confidence.

name: Fusion CPA
signal: Tax subscription landing pages and accounting-software content
services: Fusion lists tax planning and filing, accounting cleanup, controller and CFO support, and accounting-software services including QuickBooks and NetSuite work.
focus: a growing business whose accounting system needs attention
scenario: A family business is moving to a new accounting system while owners discuss distributions and a related-party property transaction. Tax work needs stable balances and a defined point at which migrated records can be used.
risk: Software migration can change account mappings without changing underlying economics. Ask who validates opening balances and which version of the ledger supports the planning analysis before approving distributions.
questions: Who signs off migrated balances and mappings?
Is software implementation part of the tax proposal?
How are related-party records reviewed after migration?
records: Old ledger export and migration mapping
deliverable: a validated opening-balance package and a separate owner-decision timetable
switch: needing system implementation and tax work to stay coordinated
alternative: Compare a software-capable accounting provider with keeping the implementation consultant and hiring a tax planner. The handoff should identify accepted balances, unresolved issues and the date planning can begin using the new system.

name: GreenGrowth CPAs
signal: Industry topic hubs, videos and downloadable guidance
services: GreenGrowth advertises tax, accounting, audit and CFO advisory across industries with complex reporting requirements, including cannabis, technology and real estate.
focus: a business requiring specialized reporting or external assurance
scenario: A regulated business needs a lender-requested financial report while its owner seeks personal tax planning. The first step is determining the exact assurance requirement and the qualifications needed for that engagement.
risk: A tax-planning proposal cannot substitute for a specified assurance engagement. Obtain the lender's written requirement and identify independence and reporting obligations before selecting the firm responsible for that work.
questions: What exact report does the lender require?
Which professional entity performs any assurance work?
How is owner tax planning separated from reporting obligations?
records: Lender reporting request and loan agreement
deliverable: a confirmed reporting specification and a separate owner-planning scope
switch: needing a specialist report in addition to ordinary tax work
alternative: Choose an appropriately qualified assurance provider when that is the actual requirement. AE can be evaluated for a separate owner-planning engagement; it should not be treated as a substitute for external assurance or industry-specific compliance responsibilities.

name: SDO CPA
signal: Tax-planning guides and remote consultation offers
services: SDO CPA publishes year-round planning and compliance for business entities, including multi-entity and intercompany considerations and property-related coordination.
focus: related entities and the records connecting them
scenario: Two partners operate a service company and a separate property entity. Intercompany transfers and owner contributions have been recorded inconsistently. Before discussing strategy, each entity's balances and ownership records need to agree.
risk: A consolidated owner view can hide discrepancies between legal entities. Require a reconciliation of transfers, loans and contributions before treating cash movement as taxable income or available distribution cash.
questions: Who reconciles intercompany balances across entities?
How are partner contributions and distributions documented?
Which business and owner returns enter the planning scope?
records: Property leases and prior K-1 schedules
deliverable: a cross-entity reconciliation and a responsibility map for partner reporting
switch: needing a coordinated review of partnership and property records
alternative: Compare a multi-entity planning engagement with a targeted reconciliation project if records are the main problem. If multiple preparers remain involved, require an agreed K-1 delivery schedule and a single record of unresolved issues.

name: Nth Degree CPAs
signal: WealthType assessment, newsletter and financial-roadmap content
services: Nth Degree publishes tax planning and preparation, bookkeeping, payroll, controller and fractional CFO services, plus valuation and financial-roadmap offerings.
focus: an owner's broader financial roadmap and reporting needs
scenario: An owner is considering hiring a controller and eventually selling the business. There is no immediate transaction, but tax decisions and management reporting are becoming more complicated. The owner needs a phased scope instead of buying every possible service at once.
risk: A roadmap needs decision dates and measurable outputs to be useful. Distinguish tax work required now from controller support and valuation projects that may belong in a later phase.
questions: Which roadmap outputs are delivered in the first phase?
When does controller or CFO support become a separate engagement?
What triggers a valuation or exit-readiness project?
records: Current close process and reporting gaps
Owner goals and target decision dates
deliverable: a phased service roadmap with approval points and separately priced work
switch: wanting clearer sequencing across tax, reporting and eventual exit needs
alternative: Compare phased proposals rather than broad promises of financial improvement. A narrowly scoped planning engagement can be the first step when the next decision is clear; a recurring finance team may fit when reporting gaps affect management every month.

name: TL;DR Accounting
signal: Private-practice tax guides and first-year practice resources
services: TL;DR Accounting markets remote accounting, reporting, tax preparation and financial coaching with a focus on therapy practices.
focus: a therapist establishing dependable financial routines
scenario: A therapist has opened a practice and uses personal funds for early expenses. The immediate job is separating business records and establishing an understandable close and filing process before the owner considers hiring or adding another activity.
risk: Early bookkeeping choices can make later review harder. Ask the provider to document owner-funded expenses and explain which information must be retained so a future advisor can understand opening balances.
questions: How are startup costs and owner-funded expenses documented?
What monthly records will I receive and retain?
When does hiring require additional payroll or advisory scope?
records: Startup receipts and owner funding history
Business accounts and practice revenue records
Formation documents and prior personal returns
deliverable: an opening-record package and a first-year close and filing calendar
switch: moving from informal personal records to a structured practice workflow
alternative: Compare a therapist-focused accounting service with a targeted setup and tax-preparation engagement. An established practice with outside investments may instead need coordinated owner planning while preserving the practice bookkeeping process.
